stem.text: The power series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n} \left(x - 1\right)^{n}}{2^{n} \left(n^{2} + 2\right)} \) has radius of convergence \( 2 \). Determine whether the series converges or diverges at \( x = -1 \), naming the test used.

answer_key.label: At \( x = -1 \) the series converges by direct comparison with \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{2}} \), because \( p = 2 > 1 \).

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x - 1\right| < 2 \), so the left endpoint is \( x = -1 \).
At \( x = -1 \), \( \frac{\left(x - 1\right)^{n}}{2^{n}} = \left(\frac{-2}{2}\right)^{n} = (-1)^{n} \), so the series becomes \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2} + 2} \).
The terms are positive and \( \frac{1}{n^{2} + 2} < \frac{1}{n^{2}} \), the terms of a convergent p-series with \( p = 2 > 1 \).
At \( x = -1 \) the series converges by direct comparison with \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{2}} \), because \( p = 2 > 1 \), so \( x = -1 \) belongs to the interval of convergence.

options.label: At \( x = -1 \) the series converges by direct comparison with \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{2}} \), because \( p = 2 > 1 \).
At \( x = -1 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the terms \( \frac{(-1)^n}{n^{2} + 2} \) alternate and shrink.
options.derivation: the factor (-1)^n produced by substituting the negative displacement -2 dropped, so the endpoint series was tested with the wrong sign pattern

options.label: At \( x = -1 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{2} + 2} \) decrease to 0.
options.derivation: the alternating series test used on the endpoint series although its terms are all positive

options.label: At \( x = -1 \) the series diverges by the p-series test, because \( p = 2 > 1 \).
options.derivation: the p-series threshold reversed, so p greater than 1 read as divergence
